Article Title: Volkswagen plans another 50,000 job cuts in biggest restructuring in 90 years
Article Text:
The latest cuts will take Volkswagen’s planned job reductions to 100,000 by 2030.

German carmaker Volkswagen is set to cut another 50,000 jobs by 2030 as part of its biggest restructuring in almost 90 years, taking the total number of positions it plans to eliminate by the end of the decade to 100,000.Volkswagen, one of the world's largest carmakers, owns brands including Audi, Porsche, Skoda, Seat, Bentley and Lamborghini. The group has been grappling with weaker sales, falling profits and intensifying competition, particularly from Chinese electric vehicle manufacturers.The company's supervisory board approved the latest workforce reduction plan on Thursday. Volkswagen had already announced in March that it would cut 50,000 jobs by 2030."A fundamental adjustment of the global workforce capability is necessary" to protect the company's competitiveness amid changing demand and rapid technological shifts, Volkswagen said, as quoted by BBC.The company said the latest round of restructuring would involve "approximately 50,000 positions - including management roles". It also plans to focus on its "most compelling vehicles" and increase production volumes for each model in an effort to reduce costs.Volkswagen chief executive Oliver Blume described the decision as a "strong signal" for the company's future, saying it was "taking responsibility for our entire workforce". Blume had told the BBC in July that Volkswagen was considering further job cuts.The carmaker is also reviewing the future of four German plants in Emden, Zwickau, Hanover and Neckarsulm, where production capacity currently exceeds demand. "Alternative uses for these plants are being assessed," Volkswagen said.The restructuring comes as Volkswagen seeks to restore profitability and remain competitive in a rapidly changing global auto industry. The group employed more than 660,000 people worldwide in 2025.Christianne Benner, president of Europe's largest industrial union IG Metall and deputy chair of Volkswagen's Supervisory Board, said the carmaker had "fought hard for good solutions" to address what she described as a "crisis situation".
Article Summary: Volkswagen is set to cut another 50,000 jobs by 2030 as part of its biggest restructuring in almost 90 years. The latest cuts will take the total number of positions it plans to eliminate by the end of the decade to 100,000. The group has been grappling with weaker sales, falling profits and intensifying competition.

Article Title: Oil heads for biggest weekly gain since July as Middle East tensions flare
Article Text:
Brent crude rose 15 cents to $95.67 a barrel, while WTI gained 26 cents to $91.56.

Oil prices edged higher on Friday and were headed for their biggest weekly gain since mid-July as escalating tensions between the US and Iran raised concerns over disruptions to crude supplies from the Middle East Brent crude futures rose 15 cents, or 0.2%, to $95.67 a barrel at 0100 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate crude gained 26 cents, or 0.3%, to $91.56.Brent was up 7.1% for the week, while WTI had gained 9.8%, putting both benchmarks on course for their strongest weekly advances since the week ended July 20.The latest gains came after US attacks this week killed and wounded dozens, including Iranian civilians, in the fiercest clashes between Washington and Tehran since July. The conflict, which began with US-Israeli strikes at the end of February, has now entered its seventh month.Concerns over the wider impact on energy infrastructure have also grown. Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz renewed warnings that Israel would "cripple" Iran's military and civilian infrastructure, including energy facilities.US Vice President JD Vance said on Thursday that Washington would not hold talks with Iran unless Tehran stops attacking commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, a key global oil transit route.Iran has also expanded its list of vessels it considers non-compliant, warning that they could face fines, confiscation or detention if they attempt to transit the strait. Iraqi vessels remain among the few ships Tehran has cleared to pass through Hormuz.Iraq, meanwhile, increased oil exports to around 2.34 million barrels per day in August from about 1.35 million bpd in July, according to two Iraqi energy officials. September exports are also expected to rise as heavy discounts and Iranian approvals for Iraqi tankers encourage buyers.Capping oil's gains, Russian President Vladimir Putin said there was still a path to a deal to end the war in Ukraine, adding that both the US and China were prepared to support a peace settlement.
Article Summary: Brent crude futures rose 15 cents, or 0.2%, to $95.67 a barrel at 0100 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate crude gained 26 cents to $91.56. Both benchmarks on course for their strongest weekly advances since July 20.

Article Title: 8th Pay Commission salary hike calculator: A Level 8 employee could earn up to Rs 28.89 lakh extra over 10 years if annual increment rises from 3% to 7% with 2.15 fitment factor
Article Text:
One issue that is likely to come up again is the annual increment rate for central government employees.

8th Pay Commission: Recommendations for higher increment rate

How 3% annual increment rate impacts salaries of central government employees

How employees’ basic pay may be impacted at 5%-7% annual increment rates

Salary calculation assumptions

The current basic pay of the Level 8 employee is Rs 47,600.

The estimated revised basic pay under the 8th CPC is calculated by multiplying the existing basic pay by a 2.15 fitment factor.

At a 3% increment rate, the annual increase is calculated on the revised basic pay.

The total salary over 10 years is calculated using the 3% annual increment.

The same revised basic pay is used to calculate the annual increment at rates ranging from 5% to 7%.

The 10-year salary under the higher increment rates is then compared with the total salary under the 3% increment.

The additional salary over 10 years is the difference between the total pay under the 5%, 6% or 7% increment and the total pay under the 3% increment.

Salary benefit in 10 years at 3% vs 5% annual increment rate

Year 1: At 3%, monthly basic is Rs 1,02,340 and annual salary is Rs 12,28,080. At 5%, monthly basic is Rs 1,02,340 and annual salary is Rs 12,28,080.

Year 10: At 3%, Rs 1,33,530 monthly and Rs 16,02,366 annually. At 5%, Rs 1,58,763 monthly and Rs 19,05,155 annually.

Salary benefit in 10 years at 3% vs 7% annual increment rate

Year 1: At 3%, monthly basic is Rs 1,02,340 and annual salary is Rs 12,28,080. At

Year 10: At 3%, Rs 1,33,530 monthly and Rs 16,02,366 annually. At 7%, Rs 1,88,148 monthly and Rs 22,57,775 annually.

8th Pay Commission news: The 8th Pay Commission is set to travel to Chennai on September 7 and 8, following its two-day stakeholders’ consultation meeting in Jaipur. During the Chennai visit, representatives of employee and pensioner organisations, along with other stakeholders, are expected to meet officials of the 8th CPC and put forward their demands on various issues.One issue that is likely to come up again is the annual increment rate for central government employees. Several major employee organisations had raised the issue prominently during the previous consultation, seeking an increase from the existing 3% rate.Employee bodies have argued that the current 3% annual increment is not sufficient to keep pace with rising expenses. Their recommendations have ranged from 5% to 7%. If such proposals are accepted, a higher increment rate of 5% or 7% would have a direct impact on the salary progression of central government employees.The National Council of the Joint Consultative Machinery (NC-JCM), the main body representing central government employees, has proposed raising the annual increment to 6% in its memorandum submitted to the 8th Pay Commission.The All India Defence Employees’ Federation (AIDEF) and the Federation of National Postal Organisations (FNPO) have also sought an annual increment rate of 6%.The All India New Pension Scheme Employees’ Federation (AINPSEF) has made the highest demand among these organisations, recommending a 7% annual increment.The Indian Railways’ Supervisors’ Association (IRTSA) has proposed a 5% annual increment rate, according to ET.To understand the effect of the existing 3% annual increment, consider a Level 1 central government employee. Under the 7th Pay Commission, the starting basic pay for this level is Rs 18,000. With a 3% annual increment, the basic pay would rise to Rs 23,500 by the end of the 10th year of the pay commission.A similar calculation for a Level 5 employee shows that a starting basic pay of Rs 29,200 under the 7th Pay Commission would increase to around Rs 38,100 by the 10th year.Basic pay is not the only component of a central government employee’s salary. Most employees also receive dearness allowance (DA), house rent allowance (HRA) and transport allowance (TPTA).Despite these additional allowances, employee associations argue that those at the lower levels can still find it difficult to manage their expenses, particularly when posted in Tier I cities. The AINSPEF has argued that a 7% annual increment could nearly double an employee’s basic salary over the course of a pay commission.To see how a higher annual increment could affect salary progression, ET considers a Level 8 employee whose current basic pay is Rs 47,600.For this comparison, assume that the 8th Pay Commission approves a 2.15 fitment factor. The employee’s basic pay can then be compared over a 10-year period under four different annual increment scenarios: 3%, 5%, 7%.To compare how different annual increment rates could affect salary progression, the calculation uses the following assumptions:The employee’s current basic pay is Rs 47,600. Applying the assumed 2.15 fitment factor gives an estimated revised basic pay of Rs 1,02,340.The salary progression under the two scenarios works out as follows:Over the 10-year period, the total pay under the 3% increment is Rs 1,40,78,561, compared with Rs 1,54,46,658 under the 5% increment.That means the higher 5% increment would result in an additional Rs 13,68,097 over 10 years.The gap becomes even wider when the annual increment is assumed to be 7%.Over 10 years, total pay under the 3% increment works out to Rs 1,40,78,561. At a 7% annual increment, the corresponding figure rises to Rs 1,69,67,703.The additional pay under the 7% scenario would therefore be Rs 28,89,143 over 10 years.These calculations illustrate how a small increase in the annual increment rate can widen the difference in basic pay for central government employees over time. However, these figures are only estimates. The actual increment rate and salary revision will be known only after the government notifies the 8th Pay Commission report.
Article Summary: The 8th Pay Commission is set to travel to Chennai on September 7 and 8, following its two-day stakeholders’ consultation meeting in Jaipur. One issue that is likely to come up again is the annual increment rate for central government employees. Several major employee organisations had raised the issue prominently during the previous consultation.

Article Title: Wrong mobile digit sent her train ticket to another passenger who cancelled it; she was deboarded at midnight, arrested and lost her job, Kerala SHRC orders Railways to pay Rs 2 lakh
Article Text:
The incident took place on July 30, 2023, when Jayasmitha was travelling on train 16348. (Image for representative purpose only)

What led to woman being deboarded at midnight

The wrong mobile number

What Kerala State Human Rights Commission ruled

You have a confirmed railway ticket, but due to a possible clerical error, your mobile number is typed wrongly, sending the reservation to someone else, who cancels the ticket. You are then deboarded from the train!That’s what happened with K Jayasmitha in Kerala who is a native of Erumapetty in Thrissur who currently resides in Thiruvananthapuram.Indian Railways has been asked to compensate her. The order followed an incident in which she was made to get off a train around midnight despite having a valid reservation. She was subsequently arrested by the Railway Protection Force (RPF) on the allegation that she was travelling without a ticket.The incident took place on July 30, 2023, when Jayasmitha was travelling on train 16348 from Wadakkanchery to Thiruvananthapuram.Jayasmitha believed she was travelling with a confirmed and valid reservation. The problem became apparent only after she boarded the train and reached the berth allotted to her, where she found another passenger occupying the seat.She had been allotted berth 41 in coach S4, but on boarding the train, she found that the same berth had been assigned to another passenger.According to her complaint, the TTE informed her that her ticket had been cancelled online and asked her to pay Rs 500 as a fine for another berth.Jayasmitha could not make the payment in cash.With the issue unresolved and the train already underway, she was left without the berth for which she had originally held a confirmed reservation.When the train reached Aluva, she was handed over to the RPF.She was treated as if she had boarded the train without a ticket deliberately, despite the fact that she had originally held a genuine confirmed reservation and had not herself cancelled it.Jayasmitha was later released on bail. The Railways subsequently withdrew the case after determining that it had been registered incorrectly.A departmental inquiry later found that a digit in the mobile number entered during the booking process had been altered on the website. As a result, the reservation message was sent to a different mobile number, following which the person who received it cancelled the ticket.Jayasmitha, however, maintained that the mistake had been made by the booking clerk. She also told the commission that she lost her government contract job because of the criminal case arising from the incident.The commission directed her to approach the government regarding the loss of employment. It also instructed the minority welfare director to take a decision on her request within one month.The Kerala State Human Rights Commission has directed the Railways to pay Rs 2 lakh in compensation.The order held the Railways responsible not only for the administrative mistake that set the incident in motion, but also for the manner in which officials dealt with the woman travelling alone after the reservation dispute arose on the train.In its order, commission chairperson Justice Alexander Thomas instructed the Railways to make the compensation payment within one month and submit written confirmation once the amount had been paid. If the compensation is not paid within six weeks, the Railways will have to pay interest at 8%.Thomas held that making a woman travelling alone leave a train at midnight amounted to wrongful action under Section 139 of the Railways Act. The commission found violations of Sections 137 and 139.The commission also observed that the manner in which Jayasmitha was treated was unfair, particularly as she lives alone without her parents. It held that the incident violated her constitutional and human right to live with dignity.The order has also allowed an inquiry to be conducted against the officials found responsible. It further permits the Southern Railway divisional railway manager to recover the compensation amount from the officials concerned, in accordance with the law.The commission has additionally instructed railway authorities to issue a circular immediately, directing officials to strictly follow Sections 137 and 139 and take necessary steps to ensure the safety of women travelling alone at night.
Article Summary: K Jayasmitha was travelling on train 16348 from Wadakkanchery to Thiruvananthapuram. She believed she was travelling with a confirmed and valid reservation. The problem became apparent only when she reached the berth allotted to her, where she found another passenger occupying the seat. She was subsequently arrested by the Railway Protection Force.

Article Title: Adobe names another India-born CEO, Anil Chakravarthy to take over after Shantanu Narayen’s 18-year run
Article Text:
Chakravarthy joined Adobe in 2020 and currently leads its customer experience orchestration business and worldwide field operations.

Adobe has named India-born executive Anil Chakravarthy as its new president and chief executive officer, succeeding Shantanu Narayen, who is stepping down after more than 18 years at the helm.The company said on Thursday that Chakravarthy will take over as CEO on December 1, while Narayen will transition to the role of executive chair.Chakravarthy currently serves as president of Adobe’s Customer Experience Orchestration business and worldwide field operations. He joined Adobe in January 2020 as executive vice president and general manager of its Digital Experience business.“I could not be more confident that Anil is the right person to lead Adobe's growth in an AI-driven era,” Narayen said, adding that he looked forward to working with Chakravarthy in his new role as executive chair, as quoted by PTI.Chakravarthy, an alumnus of the Indian Institute of Technology (Banaras Hindu University), Varanasi, has held several leadership roles at Adobe. He took on responsibility for the company’s worldwide field operations in September 2020 and was promoted to president of Digital Experience and worldwide field operations in December 2021.Before joining Adobe, Chakravarthy served as CEO of enterprise cloud data management company Informatica for four years.He had joined Informatica in 2013 as an executive vice president and previously held senior roles at Symantec, VeriSign and McKinsey & Company.He holds a Bachelor of Technology in Computer Science and Engineering from IIT (Banaras Hindu University), along with a master's degree and PhD from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology.Meanwhile, David Wadhwani, president of Adobe’s Creativity and Productivity business and one of the contenders for the CEO position, announced his departure after five years with the company.“As much as Adobe means to me, I've decided this is the right moment for me to start a new chapter, and it's a great moment for Adobe to do the same as Anil steps into the CEO role,” Wadhwani said in a LinkedIn post.Chakravarthy, in his own post, said he was “honoured and incredibly excited” about what lies ahead, highlighting Adobe’s customers, employees and AI innovation as his priorities.Adobe's leadership transition comes as the software giant pushes further into artificial intelligence and seeks to expand its growth in an increasingly AI-driven technology landscape.
Article Summary: Anil Chakravarthy, an alumnus of the Indian Institute of Technology (Banaras Hindu University), Varanasi, will take over as CEO on December 1. Shantanu Narayen, who is stepping down after more than 18 years at the helm, will transition to the role of executive chair.

Article Title: 'AI will kill digital': Axis Bank head Sameer Shetty calls ‘Zero-Ops’ north star
Article Text:
Sameer Shetty, group head, digital business and transformation and strategic platforms at Axis Bank

Axis Bank

has lined up 19 launches for the upcoming Global Fintech Fest.

Sameer Shetty

, group head – digital business and transformation and strategic platforms at Axis Bank, speaks about how technology is reducing human intervention, improving

customer experience

and enhancing safety. Shetty, a former partner at McKinsey, has worked with financial institutions across India, Southeast Asia and the Middle East.

What was the thinking behind using the bank-within-a-bank concept for digital?

Do you use it to provide differentiated digital-only products?

How does digital help in customer acquisition?

How do you work with Freecharge?

Where all are you using AI in the bank?

What is the progress on the unified lending interface and credit on UPI?

What is the bank doing to prevent digital fraud?

How is the bank using the Account Aggregator platform, where you can access details of other accounts?

We made digital a self-contained business because it requires different skills from branch banking. Branch banking depends on physical distribution; digital depends on technology, design and simple customer journeys. Bringing technology, product, design, marketing and risk together lets us build and take products to market faster. We have a 50-member design team, many from outside banking, and nearly 300 engineers who build in-house.But this is not a separate bank. What we build is also used across the bank. A personal-loan customer can apply through the app, branch, salesperson or DSA, using essentially the same underlying technology. The aim is to give digital banking the capabilities to operate end-to-end while making those capabilities available to the wider bank.It is not just an alternative channel; it is built to design and incubate truly digital-first and digital-only products, like one-click pre-approved personal loans, created specifically with native digital journeys in mind. We operate under a strict definition where "digital business" refers exclusively to end-to-end, straight-through journeys where both customer acquisition and processing happen with zero human intervention.This is fundamentally distinct from assisted journeys, where a salesperson or branch initiates the lead even if the back end is automated, or traditional physical, paper-based processes. Because only pure, unassisted D2C transactions flow into our digital unit's dedicated balance sheet and P&L, and our direct digital marketing costs are self-contained, we can cleanly measure our distinct cost structures, unit economics, loan volumes, and product-level fee and interest yields without blurring them into the wider branch network.Acquiring new-to-bank customers has not scaled to the extent we would like it to. It accounts for under 5% of fresh savings-account acquisitions. Its real strength is deepening existing relationships. Around 25% of personal loans are sourced end-to-end through the app, rising to 55% for fixed deposits and nearly 70% for mutual funds.Digital is also the primary engine for select lifecycle products, with over 85% of credit-card EMI conversions happening on the app. So while new-to-bank acquisition remains distribution-led, digital drives large-scale, self-service adoption among existing customers.We house our entire in-house engineering team, nearly 300 strong, within Freecharge to take advantage of its native fintech DNA. Traditionally, banking technology teams relied heavily on external vendors rather than building software themselves, which made it challenging to attract specialised engineering talent with standard banking organisational structures. Freecharge gives us a tech-first environment, modern organisational design and technical career growth paths that attract top developers and product builders who might never consider working directly inside a traditional bank.Operationally, the engagement functions much like a vendor relationship: we commission specific projects and pay Freecharge accordingly. However, by regulation and design, Freecharge is a 100% captive sister company dedicated entirely to Axis Bank. They do not build or service products for anyone else, ensuring complete alignment with our roadmap as they develop our proprietary digital architectures, journeys and native products in-house.We are using AI across customer service, operations, risk and technology, with “zero-ops” as our north star. Conversational AI handles about 10% of inbound calls and is scaling into outbound collections.In current-account re-KYC, AI validates complex documents at branches, cutting NFTR (not first time right) from over 70% to around 25% and review hops from an average of 3–4 to roughly 1.5. We are extending this to lending/MSME onboarding, where AI reads unstructured and handwritten documents, extracts data and pre-fills applications, replacing 20-minute forms with targeted questions. AI also streamlines risk/compliance checks, audits, Change Management Committee/Project Management Committee notes and CCTV monitoring. AI is not restricted to one part. One of the things AI will do is ‘kill digital’.In technology, AI supports application builds, vibe coding, and the use of team transcripts and emails to build business requirement documents. Our Thrive portal was built in just two weeks using AI; meeting transcripts/emails generate first-draft BRDs, leaving teams to handle only the incremental 30%. While AI-led testing and InfoSec remain throughput challenges, our goal is an end-to-end AI-driven IT lifecycle. We are also exploring customer-facing AI, but cautiously until we reach 100% comfort and safety.We were one of the first banks to go live on ULI and still have one of the highest market shares, processing four-digit crore amounts every month through its APIs. ULI, built by the RBI Innovation Hub, aggregates multiple lending-related data sources through APIs, including PAN and land records, which we use for SME lending. It is a bit like what the Account Aggregator does.We had also launched credit line on UPI two years ago but subsequently withdrew it. The biggest challenge is that, unlike a credit card, a loan cannot offer an interest-free period. RBI rules require interest to apply from Day 0. Without the 30-day-or-so interest-free period that makes credit cards attractive, customers have little reason to choose credit on UPI over a card.Over the past 18 months, we have tightened digital security by replacing internet-banking OTPs with in-app mobile PINs, sharply reducing fraud, and adding Aadhaar Face Auth across 6–7 journeys, including personal-loan disbursals. Lock FD prevents online FD closure and requires Face Auth to unlock.Our Safety Center lets customers switch off internet banking/UPI, block fund transfers and set controls such as a 10 PM–6 AM transaction block. SMS Shield verifies bank messages, while high-risk transactions, such as significant transfers by senior citizens to first-time recipients, can trigger alerts and confirmation.The bigger challenge is scams such as digital arrest and investment fraud, where customers themselves authorise payments. We can flag and verify such transactions, but ultimately customers must recognise when they are being manipulated.We are using Account Aggregator for both lending and personal finance management (PFM). About 2 million customers use our PFM feature out of our 16–17 million monthly active users. Customers can link external bank, mutual fund and broking accounts for a consolidated view of their finances.Currently, we provide detailed categorisation of our own debit-card, credit-card and UPI spends over six months to a year, and plan to extend this to external savings accounts. Credit-card data is not yet available through the aggregator. As a Financial Information User, we securely store retrieved data, giving us the capability to build features such as cross-bank transaction search, though customers currently have to view each bank separately. We strictly follow purpose-bound consent. If data is accessed for PFM, we cannot use that same data for lending decisions.

Govt flagged what it described as an incorrect depiction of India’s boundaries on AI company Anthropic’s website following a complaint.In a notice dated Sept 1, govt said it received a complaint regarding the alleged incorrect depiction of India’s external boundaries in a presentation titled ‘Where Claude is Used in India’. The presentation was reportedly shown during an online AI training session conducted via Zoom.According to the notice, the map used in the presentation appeared to have been sourced from the Anthropic Economics Index. Govt also examined a map available on Anthropic’s India contact page and found similar issues.The notice said the Union territory of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh had been depicted incorrectly, shown using dotted lines. “The state of Arunachal Pradesh has also been depicted with dotted lines. The external boundaries of India have been depicted incorrectly in the subject map,” the Survey of India notice said.An examination of Anthropic’s Economic Index webpage found the territories of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh were depicted incorrectly. In addition, the Andaman and Nicobar Islands and Lakshadweep Islands were not shown on the map, the notice observed. Any incorrect depiction of the map is an offence punishable with up to six months in jail or a fine, or both, the notice said.When TOI reached out to Anthropic, its spokesperson said, “We’ve updated the map on our website for Indian users. The issue came from a standard third-party map dataset, which we corrected as soon as we were made aware
Article Summary: Govt flagged what it described as an incorrect depiction of India’s boundaries on AI company Anthropic's website following a complaint. The Union territory of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh had been depicted incorrectly, shown using dotted lines. The presentation was reportedly shown during an online AI training session conducted via Zoom.

Article Title: Sebi to tweak CAS, change method for derivative trade
Article Text:
The decision comes exactly a month after CAS was rolled out on Aug 3

MUMBAI: Markets regulator Sebi on Thursday said it will revise the settlement price mechanism for derivatives contracts for Closing Auction Session (CAS). The decision comes exactly a month after CAS was rolled out on Aug 3. Sebi will soon come out with a consultation paper for revising the mechanism, a release from the regulator said.During the past month, introduction of CAS created significant market volatility and at times led to closing price discrepancies between two exchanges. In contrast, globally, CAS is used for a better closing price discovery. Sebi had shifted to CAS from the earlier system of Volume-weighted Average Price (V-WAP) for all stocks traded in the derivatives segment.Over the past month, Sebi chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey had reiterated on at least two occasions that the regulator would not change the CAS process but was willing to tweak it after looking into trading data.On Aug 20, Sebi had penalised Copthall, a JP Morgan entity registered as an FPI in India, and Mansi Broking, a domestic broker, for manipulating sensex levels during CAS on Aug 13, a weekly F&O contracts expiry day.Then again Aug 27, a day for monthly F&O contracts expiry, there was huge price volatility in sensex and banked contracts during CAS. On Thursday also sensex saw some sharp volatility during CAS."The framework for CAS was introduced following extensive stakeholder consultations and detailed policy deliberations," the Sebi release said. "Since its implementation, Sebi has closely engaged with various stakeholders, including stock exchanges, brokers, proprietary traders, software vendors, mutual funds, industry associations and FPIs, with a view to facilitating smooth implementation and addressing operational and other issues arising during the initial period of adoption. "The release said that the regulator had been closely monitoring the functioning of CAS and its impact on the market during the first month of its operation. "During this period, Sebi has received feedback and suggestions from various market participants and stakeholders through multiple channels, including social media and other media platforms. Among the issues raised, a significant area of feedback relates to the determination of settlement prices of derivative contracts on expiry based on the closing pr ice determined through CAS. "
Article Summary: The decision comes exactly a month after CAS was rolled out on Aug 3. Sebi will soon come out with a consultation paper for revising the mechanism. introduction of CAS created significant market volatility and at times led to closing price discrepancies between two exchanges.

Article Title: Govt eyes auto cos-led model to fix EV charging on highways
Article Text:
The ministry has identified 60 priority corridors for electrification

NEW DELHI: Govt wants automakers to take greater responsibility for fixing gaps in India's electric vehicle EV charging network. Speaking at Siam's annual session, Kamran Rizvi, secretary, ministry of heavy industries, said nearly half of mapped charging stations were non-functional, underscoring a major consumer pain point as EV adoption expands.The ministry has identified 60 priority corridors for electrification and has shared the list with Siam. Rizvi suggested the industry body could coordinate with automakers to divide these stretches among OEMs (original equipment manufacturers), which would then work towards deploying charging infrastructure on their assigned highways."We should be able to saturate all the important highways in the next two to three years," he said.The proposal comes as govt gradually reduces direct subsidies for EV purchases and looks to industry to shoulder a larger part of the ecosystem build-out. Rizvi pointed to electric three-wheelers, where penetration has reached around 50%, as evidence that some segments can continue growing without perpetual subsidy support.The heavy industries ministry also has a Rs 2,000 crore corpus for charging infrastructure, which Rizvi said could be extended to automakers for deployment.Charging depots are also planned across 160 cities to support the electrification of buses.Rizvi said charging should be easier to scale than conventional fuel retailing because it does not require the same upstream supply chain. "Charging is a standalone business," he said, urging automakers to play a more direct role not just in installing chargers, but also in ensuring they remain functional and dependable for consumers.
Article Summary: Govt wants automakers to take greater responsibility for fixing gaps in India's electric vehicle EV charging network. Nearly half of mapped charging stations were non-functional, underscoring a major consumer pain point as EV adoption expands. Ministry has identified 60 priority corridors for electrification and has shared the list with Siam.

Article Title: Nvidia’s price hike plan may raise India’s AI infra costs
Article Text:
India’s AI infrastructure push could get more expensive

NEW DELHI: India’s AI infrastructure push could get more expensive. Nvidia’s reported plan to raise AI server prices by around 15% from next year is expected to increase deployment costs for GPU cloud providers, data-centre operators and companies building large compute clusters, with industry executives warning that some of the increase may ultimately be passed on to customers.The impact could be particularly significant as India scales up AI compute capacity across private data centres, cloud platforms and govt-backed programmes. Higher hardware costs could force operators to reassess expansion plans, delay fresh capacity additions or explore alternative chip architectures.“Nvidia’s pricing is driven largely by demand and component costs, especially memory, which remains tight and is projected to rise through 2027,” said Ishan Talathi, founder and CEO of CloudPe. Talathi said Nvidia had already raised prices of its RTX Pro 6000 series from $13,250 to $16,000 earlier this month, an increase of 20.8% in two months.“For an AI cloud platform like CloudPe, where GPU servers are among the biggest capex items, this translates into a 10-12% increase in overall deployment costs,” he said. CloudPe expects GPU cloud pricing in India to rise by 10-15% over the next 12-18 months unless memory supply improves or alternative architectures gain traction.And, the pressure is not restricted to GPUs. Amit Chaurasia, data infrastructure expert and founder of Dataneers, said sharp increases in prices of memory and storage components were already affecting enterprise buying decisions.“It’s not GPUs but HDDs and RAMs that have quadrupled in price. This is an unprecedented rise,” Chaurasia said, adding that customers were delaying purchases in the hope that prices would ease. While large enterprises may have the financial capacity to absorb higher costs, smaller companies could be more vulnerable. Chaurasia said SMEs were more likely to defer technology investments, while higher hardware costs could have a cascading effect across sectors as technology becomes an increasingly important input for businesses.
Article Summary: N Nvidia’s reported plan to raise AI server prices by around 15% from next year. Industry executives warn that some of the increase may ultimately be passed on to customers. Higher hardware costs could force operators to reassess expansion plans, delay fresh capacity additions or explore alternative chip architectures.

Article Title: EV shift puts auto parts MSMEs under pressure
Article Text:
India's shift towards electric mobility and tech-intensive vehicles is exposing a capability gap

CHENNAI: India's shift towards electric mobility and tech-intensive vehicles is exposing a capability gap among auto component manufacturers, particularly MSMEs, even as imports of batteries, power electronics, embedded software and advanced electronics rise.Domestic OEM sourcing of auto components grew 16% to Rs 6.6 lakh crore in FY26, while component exports reached Rs 2.1 lakh crore. But imports are growing faster, with China accounting for about 36% of India's auto component imports, according to a study by Vector Consulting Group.The challenge is significant for MSMEs, which account for around 80% of India's auto parts producers. While advanced engineering, electronics, embedded software and systems integration are increasingly critical to competitiveness, fewer than half of MSME suppliers are estimated to have these capabilities. Embedded software capability exists in only about 10% of suppliers and systems integration and product development capabilities in around 14%."India's automotive opportunity will depend on how quickly capability can be built across the supplier ecosystem," Ravindra Patki, Managing Partner, Vector Consulting Group, told TOI. "Policy support has an important role in creating the right environment, but it cannot by itself close the capability gap."The financial constraints of smaller suppliers make the transition harder. Inventory levels can reach 60 days in some cases, locking up working capital, while EBITDA margins remain around 12%. Only about 10% of suppliers are estimated to have the financial capacity to invest consistently in technology, engineering and product development.
Article Summary: India's shift towards electric mobility and tech-intensive vehicles is exposing a capability gap among auto component manufacturers, particularly MSMEs. Domestic OEM sourcing of auto components grew 16% to Rs 6.6 lakh crore in FY26. China accounts for about 36% of India's auto component imports.

Article Title: Can Ratan Tata’s inherited shares go to his charities?
Article Text:
Ratan bequeathed his holding to two charitable vehicles he set up

MUMBAI: The Maharashtra charity commissioner validated the 1989 transfer of 833 Tata Sons shares from the Navajbai Ratan Tata Trust (NRTT) to Naval Tata—and in doing so, surfaced a little-known condition that’s attached to the deal: the shares could be transferred or bequeathed only to the holder’s own relatives, and not to third parties.Naval split the shares among his wife Simone and his three sons, Ratan, Jimmy and Noel—meaning the restriction followed the shares down the family line.Nearly four decades on, that condition has taken on fresh weight over the fate of the Tata Sons shares Ratan inherited from his father.Ratan bequeathed his holding to two charitable vehicles he set up: the Ratan Tata Endowment Fund (RTEF) and the Ratan Tata Endowment Trust (RTET). Simone passed her shares to her son Noel and his three children; Jimmy and Noel still hold theirs.Ratan’s shares remain part of his estate, administered by his executors, including two half-sisters Shireen and Deanna Jejeebhoy.RTEF and RTET are separate legal entities—third parties, not blood relatives. Ratan’s bequest to the two foundations thus clashes directly with the family-only condition. Wednesday’s order, signed by commissioner Amogh Kaloti, said NRTT’s trustees “are at liberty to take appropriate steps” if Ratan had bequeathed shares to charitable institutions breaching conditions attached to the original transfer.The order cites Naval Tata’s “express undertaking” that his children would “transfer or bequeath the shares to their own relatives and not to a third party. ”NRTT’s trustees are Noel, Venu Srinivasan, Vijay Singh and JN Mistry. RTET’s trustees include Noel, Shireen and Deanna.People familiar with the matter said the estate can seek clarity from the Bombay high court on the restriction and its bearing on Ratan’s bequest, transferring the shares to RTEF and RTET only after that. One person said the charity commissioner lacked judicial authority to compel a transfer to a family member or override a private will, arguing that the charitable bequest should stand if it reflected Ratan’s stated wishes. Alternatively, members of Naval Tata’s family can buy the shares, with the proceeds going to the two foundations as Ratan’s will envisaged.Any such transfer would require Tata Sons to be valued—shares would have to change hands at fair value, not what’s stated in book value. Under Ratan’s will, RTEF gets 70% of his holding and RTET the remaining 30%. Naval had bought the 833 shares—face value Rs 1,000 each— for Rs 15.9 lakh, paying Rs 1,914 apiece based on a wealth-tax valuation.Ratan’s stake is small in numerical terms. But Tata Sons is the holding company at the heart of the Tata conglomerate, and its shares are closely guarded. The 1989 restriction could now decide how this small but symbolically important holding changes hands.
Article Summary: The Maharashtra charity commissioner validated the 1989 transfer of 833 Tata Sons shares from the Navajbai Ratan Tata Trust (NRTT) to Naval Tata. In doing so, it surfaced a little-known condition that’s attached to the deal: the shares could be transferred or bequeathed only to the holder's own relatives, and not to third parties.

Article Title: 'Are we slaves to other people?' Kenya President orders Tata Chemicals to end operations after 100 years
Article Text: Kenya President William Ruto on Thursday said he had ordered Tata Chemicals to stop operations in the country, questioning, "are we slaves to other people?"Ruto said the government would bring in two new companies to take over Tata Chemicals’ operations, alleging that the company had failed to bring sufficient investment and industrial development to the region."That ⁠Tata company ... had that contract for 100 years. They have not built anything in Kajiado, they have not built any factory in Kajiado,"Ruto said during a visit to Kajiado in southern Kenya, according to Reuters."We ‌have said we will bring a new company and... they should put a big glass company ⁠here in Kajiado. And another company to make chemicals here in Kajiado. Are we slaves to other people?" he added.In late July, Tata said the Kenyan government had ordered its unit, Tata Chemical Limited, to suspend operations at the Magadi Soda factory. The company also suspended exports of soda ash from the facility.
Article Summary: Kenyan President William Ruto says he has ordered Tata Chemicals to stop operations in the country. Ruto said the government would bring in two new companies to take over Tata Chemical’s operations. In late July, Tata said the Kenyan government had ordered its unit, Tata Chemical Limited, to suspend operations.

Article Title: US-Venezuela's historic deal: Will Americans get cheaper gas now?
Article Text:
Will Americans get cheaper gas now

What the deal means for US gas prices

Why cheaper petrol may not come quickly

Will Americans actually see cheaper gas?

US President Donald Trump is betting that his Venezuela oil deal will “substantially lower gas prices for all Americans”. But whether the arrangement can deliver cheaper fuel at US pumps, and how quickly, remains uncertain. Days earlier Trump said that the US would use Venezuelan crude controlled through a deal with a private company to replenish the Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR).The agreement would give Washington access to oil fields said to contain one-fifth of Venezuela’s crude reserves, providing a stable supply of low-cost oil while helping rebuild the depleted federal stockpile.A White House official further added that oil would be flowing to the market by the end of the year, helping bring down gasoline prices.But the deal is unlikely to translate into an immediate increase in oil available to American motorists. It could take months before it produces new barrels, while the administration has not explained exactly how the Venezuelan crude would be procured. Analysts have also warned that future elections in the US and Venezuela could put the arrangement at risk.Trump has put Venezuela’s vast oil reserves at the centre of an agreement aimed at reviving the country’s struggling oil industry and attracting fresh investment.Venezuela’s interim President Delcy Rodriguez said the energy pact would run for 25 years.Under the arrangement, the US government and an unnamed private operator in Venezuela have set up a new company with rights to untapped oil fields for 100 years.Rodriguez said the agreement aims to raise Venezuela’s oil production to 1.5 million barrels per day. The deal covers 17 fields with a proven potential of 65 billion barrels, according to her statement.The agreement could bring $100 billion in investment into Venezuela’s oil industry and generate more than $209 billion in taxes for Caracas.The US government also plans to take a 35% passive stake in North American Blue Energy Partners, owned by Venezuelan businessman Alejandro Betancourt, The Wall Street Journal reported on Saturday, citing people involved in the negotiations.Trump is trying to bring gasoline prices below $4 a gallon while the US oil reserve is severely depleted.More than 128 million barrels have been released from strategic salt caverns on the Gulf Coast in an effort to mitigate the impact of the monthslong closure of the Strait of Hormuz. Oil levels at the sites have fallen to their lowest since autumn 1982.The Trump administration has repeatedly blamed former President Joe Biden for draining the reserve. But stocks have fallen further despite Trump’s pledge to replenish them “right to the top”.“I think they probably see this as a plausible mechanism for both stimulating the Venezuelan industry and bringing [oil] into the country,” Joseph Majkut, an energy expert told WSJ.The Trump administration said the deal “secures our energy dominance for the next century—all at zero cost to the United States”. It said the arrangement would ensure a stable supply of low-cost oil that could facilitate the refilling of the federal stockpile.But even if the deal starts delivering Venezuelan crude, that does not mean the SPR can be rebuilt quickly. The reserve currently holds about 286 million barrels, compared with its authorised capacity of 714 million barrels.The White House says oil will begin flowing to the market by the end of the year. A White House official also said that if the company scales as planned, the US could add 50 million barrels to its strategic reserves every year.But the timing of those barrels remains uncertain. It could take months before the deal produces new supplies, and the administration has yet to spell out exactly how the purchases will be funded and carried out.The depleted SPR also means that any new Venezuelan supply would first have to help rebuild a stockpile that is far below capacity. Even if the plan is successfully implemented, restoring the reserve to its authorised 714 million barrels would take years.The energy department had previously used proceeds from crude sales to acquire new barrels. But before Trump’s re-election, that account was essentially depleted, analysts at energy analysis firm Rapidan Energy Group noted at the time.Congress last year appropriated just $171 million to begin refilling the stockpile, compared with the $20 billion Wright said was needed.Wright had complained last year that the GOP-led Congress would not give the Trump administration the billions of dollars needed to fill the reserves.In January, a few days after the Trump administration seized Venezuelan strongman Nicolas Maduro, Wright said he was looking at “creative ways in which we do deals with private businesses that we can generate oil without any government cash and put it in the Reserve.”
Article Summary: The White House says oil will begin flowing to the market by the end of the year. But the deal is unlikely to translate into an immediate increase in oil available to American motorists. It could take months before the deal produces new supplies, and the administration has yet to spell out exactly how the purchases will be funded and carried out.

Article Title: Trump’s face debuts on US currency, $1 coins run ‘out of stock’ within hours
Article Text:
Trump’s face debuts on US currency, $1 coins run ‘out of stock’ within hours

Trump coin out of stock

Special law for Trump's portrait

It’s America’s 250th birthday, and Donald Trump is making sure he gets a spot on the souvenir.A new $1 coin marking the anniversary went on sale Wednesday with the president’s portrait on one side and the Great Seal of the United States on the other.The coins, issued by the US mint, can be used as legal tender. But their launch has also attracted criticism because federal law bars the depiction of a living president on US currency, although there are provisions allowing the Treasury Secretary to authorise special coins in certain circumstances.The coin’s design features Trump’s visage as “heads”, while the Great Seal of the United States serves as “tails”. Trump’s portrait carries the inscriptions “IN GOD WE TRUST” and “LIBERTY”, while “1776 (tilde) 2026” appears below his face.The reverse shows the Great Seal, with a bald eagle holding arrows in one claw and an olive branch in the other. A banner held in its beak carries the words “E PLURIBUS UNUM," Latin for "out of many, one.”The design received approval this year from the US Commission of Fine Arts, whose members were appointed by Trump. The president had earlier called the idea of putting his face on a coin “very unusual”, but said he was “honored by it.”The US mint said the coins were struck to “honor 250 years of great American heritage.”The coins went on sale at noon Wednesday, but appeared to be out of stock by the afternoon.A roll of 25 coins costs $61, while a bag of 100 costs $154.50. At the same time, some special-issue coins had been randomly placed among the rolls and bags.The mint’s website later stated, “This item is available to be ordered now, but it is not currently in stock. Additional inventory is being made.”The 100-coin bag was listed as unavailable, while the 25-coin roll carried the same message shortly after 3pm.Just after 12.30pm, visitors to the website were placed in a waiting area with an estimated wait time of one hour. Purchases were limited to two per household until 2pm on Thursday, with buyers given 10 minutes to complete their orders.The website also warned, “Product availability is not guaranteed.” Furthermore, the coins would also be found in circulation, with the authority urging people to "check your pocket change.”Among the coins, 250,000 have been given a special-issue “July 4th” privy mark. Mint said that these coins were randomly included in the rolls and bags because they were struck on July 4, the anniversary of the Declaration of Independence.Describing this as a “special offering”, the mint said, “250,000 Semiquincentennial President Donald J. Trump $1 Coins with a special-issue ‘July 4th’ privy mark have been randomly included in the Rolls & Bags. These coins were struck on July 4th.”Although the coin has a gold appearance, it is made from a mix of copper, zinc, manganese and nickel. Part of the additional cost of commemorative coins goes towards “organizations and projects that benefit the community”, according to the mint’s website.The use of Trump’s image on the coin comes despite US law prohibiting the display of a sitting president or living former president on US currency.In anticipation of America’s 250th anniversary, however, Congress passed the Circulating Collectible Coin Redesign Act. The legislation allows the US Treasury to mint special $1 coins to mark the event.The law also states, “No head and shoulders portrait or bust of any person, living or dead, and no portrait of a living person may be included in the design on the reverse of specified coins.”Trump’s portrait appears on the front of the coin, rather than the reverse, appearing to comply with the law.The treasury secretary also has authority in some circumstances to approve the minting and issuance of special coins.The only other time a living president was featured on a US coin was in 1926, when Calvin Coolidge appeared on a half dollar marking the 150th anniversary of the signing of the Declaration of Independence, according to the mint.The coin is also part of a wider series of branding efforts associated with Trump’s second term that have become tangled up in lawsuits.These include moves to put Trump’s name on the Kennedy Center and the US Institute of Peace, as the president seeks to leave his stamp on history and Washington, DC.CNN reached out to the Treasury Department for information on the coins’ availability and the number of orders placed. It also sought information on where the surcharge money from the coins will go.
Article Summary: $1 coin features Donald Trump's portrait on one side, Great Seal of the United States on the other. The coins went on sale at noon Wednesday, but appeared to be out of stock by the afternoon. The use of Trump's image on the coin comes despite US law prohibiting the display of a sitting president or living former president on US currency.

Article Title: Oil price today: Crude continues to trade beyond $95 per barrel amid Hormuz supply tensions
Article Text:
Oil price today

Trump says US ready for further attacks

Global supply efforts continue

Oil prices edged lower on Thursday after a volatile session, as investors assessed the latest US-Iran strikes and their impact on oil supplies through the Strait of Hormuz.Brent crude stood at $95.33 a barrel, down 30 cents or 0.31% while WTI or West Texas Intermediate was trading at $90.88 a barrel, down 13 cents or 0.14%, around 7:30 am IST.This comes after both benchmarks saw sharp swings over the previous session, rising by as much as $2 a barrel before falling by up to $1. Their session highs were the highest since July 24, while Brent eventually settled 1% higher.A key focus for the market remained the Strait of Hormuz, where shipping activity has stayed below its usual level. Four commodity vessels transited the waterway on Wednesday, compared with a 10-day average of around 13, according to preliminary shipping data from Kpler, cited by Reuters.The waterway has effectively seen shipping traffic shut down since the war began with joint US-Israeli strikes on Iranian targets in late February. Before the conflict, the strait carried about a fifth of global oil and LNG consumed.The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said the latest US attacks would further restrict traffic through the strait. Iran has also added more ships to the list of vessels it considers non-compliant and subject to fines, confiscation or detention if they attempt to sail through the waterway.Two oil tankers were hit by sea mines and disabled while attempting to transit the strait, Iran's Revolutionary Guards said on Wednesday in a statement shared by state media.The latest escalation has come in the seventh month of the US-Iran war, with the latest attacks marking the biggest exchange of fire between Tehran and Washington since July.US forces struck Iran's southern coast, while Iran fired on American bases across the region.US President Donald Trump said on Wednesday that the renewed US campaign against Iran would not continue for "too long". He also said US forces had targeted Iran's radar and missile systems."We took out all of the new equipment that they tried to build along the ‌Strait ⁠of Hormuz - some defensive, some offensive ... It was a very heavy attack last night, and we're prepared to do another one any time we want," Trump said.Despite the restrictions on traffic, the US said 17 million barrels of oil transited the Strait of Hormuz on Monday. It described this as the largest volume of crude to pass through the waterway since the US-Israeli war on Iran began.The disruption to shipping has raised concerns over world oil supplies, prompting nations worldwide to try to limit price rises by finding alternative sources of supply and relying on their reserves.Those reserves have also dwindled.The latest attacks have added another layer of uncertainty for oil markets already facing restricted movement through the Strait of Hormuz. Prices remained highly volatile during Wednesday's trading, with both Brent and WTI repeatedly moving between gains and losses before Brent ended the session higher.On Thursday, however, both benchmarks moved lower as investors assessed the uncertainty surrounding further military strikes and the potential disruption to supplies from the Middle East.
Article Summary: Brent crude was trading at $95.33 a barrel on Thursday, down 30 cents or 0.31%. WTI or West Texas Intermediate was at $90.88 a barrel, down 13 cents or0.14%. Both benchmarks saw sharp swings over the previous session, rising by as much as $2 a barrel.

Article Title: Dire straits: Brand on the run as Trump suggests Hormuz can be renamed in his honor
Article Text:
Trump’s latest push to rename the Strait of Hormuz adds another chapter to his growing campaign of political branding and geographic renaming

TOI correspondent from Washington:

Donald Trump has rescued a canal, invaded a country, conquered a gulf, annexed a lake -- at least on American maps -- and put his name on a performing-arts center. He now appears to have set his sights on the hottest waterway on the planet.The MAGA boss suggested on his social media account on Wednesday that the Strait of Hormuz could be renamed the “Trump Strait” -- because if you cannot solve a problem, you can at least rename it.The proposal is the latest addition to what has become an extraordinary Trump-era renaming and branding binge. In January 2025, Trump ordered the Gulf of Mexico renamed the Gulf of America for US federal purposes. Last week he signed an executive order changing Lake Ontario to Lake America, saying the US had been treated badly by Canada. He then helpfully suggested that the Atlantic or Pacific could be next, saying, “We have a gulf and we have a lake…Now all we need is an ocean. ”The President, someone jibed, appears to be collecting bodies of water like refrigerator magnets.The joke became even better when Google Maps and Apple Maps fell in line.Google changed Lake Ontario to Lake America for US users over the weekend. Apple followed on Tuesday. Canadians, however, continue to see Lake Ontario and users elsewhere may see both names. In other words, the lake has acquired the geographic equivalent of dual citizenship.The tech companies' compliance prompted criticism from illuminati who argue that private corporations should not allow political pressure to dictate historical and geographic nomenclature. MapQuest, an internet relic many Americans had forgotten existed, refused to make the change and suddenly discovered the most effective marketing strategy in Silicon Valley: stand up to Trump. Its downloads reportedly surged, giving it the kind reception normally reserved for rock bands that haven’t toured for a long time or sports legends making a comeback.There is also an awkward business joke buried underneath all this. Trump built his political persona partly on branding himself as a master businessman, but his corporate record includes repeated failures and bankruptcies in hotels and casinos; His casino empire alone went through multiple Chapter 11 restructurings. Trump-branded ventures have also included products and licensing deals that did not last.Late-night television has naturally treated Trump's naming obsession as premium material. The Atlantic, meanwhile, took the joke to its logical conclusion in a satirical vision of a future America in which everything is renamed “America” or “Trump,” leaving citizens unable to distinguish between brands of products, goods, and structures.Political analysts however see a serious calculation behind what many consider trolling. The renaming campaign sure is presidential theater -- cheap to stage, impossible for the internet and tv to resist, and almost guaranteed to ignite social media. But it also serves to distract people from more pressing issues -- such as cost of living and democracy going down the tubes.
Article Summary: Trump suggested on his social media account on Wednesday that the Strait of Hormuz could be renamed the “Trump Strait” The proposal is the latest addition to what has become an extraordinary Trump-era renaming and branding binge. In January 2025, Trump ordered the Gulf of Mexico renamed the Gulf Of America for US federal purposes.

Article Title: 'Stay away from Iran': US warns countries & companies as war escalates
Article Text:
Trump administration’s latest push to tighten pressure on Iran as the war escalates

US treasury secretary Scott Bessent has warned countries and businesses against supporting Iran, saying Washington is considering sanctions targeting airlines, maritime activity and digital assets as Washington expands its economic pressure campaign amid escalating hostilities.“We’re having fulsome talks with anyone supporting Iran,” Bessent said in an interview with Fox News, adding that Washington would “systematically take out bad actors.”Speaking on potential targets for further sanctions, Bessent pointed to airlines, maritime activity and digital assets, indicating that the US pressure campaign could extend beyond traditional banking and oil measures.“No one should support this regime,” he said. “My message to everyone is to stay away.”The warning comes as the Trump administration pushes its Operation Economic Outcast campaign, seeking to pressure Iran's remaining trading and financial partners to choose between doing business with Tehran and retaining access to the US financial system.The latest escalation follows a monthlong lull in fighting. Iran fired on US allies in the Gulf early Wednesday after a night of American bombardment, which Iranian officials said included a deadly strike on a wedding party.Fighting intensified after the US military struck Iranian rocket launchers on an island in the Strait of Hormuz, saying Iran planned to use them to deploy mines in the waterway. Iran retaliated with missile attacks on US bases in Jordan, which were intercepted.Iran also launched drones at Kuwait, while the UAE and Bahrain reported intercepting incoming Iranian attacks. In Iraq, Kurdish authorities said they intercepted 10 explosive-laden drones near Irbil.
Article Summary: US treasury secretary Scott Bessent warns countries and businesses against supporting Iran. He says Washington is considering sanctions targeting airlines, maritime activity and digital assets. The warning comes as the Trump administration pushes its Operation Economic Outcast campaign to pressure Iran's remaining trading and financial partners.

Article Title: Uber lays off 3,300 employees as it restructures for faster growth
Article Text:
File photo: An Uber logo is displayed at the company's headquarters in San Francisco (Picture credit: AP)

Uber seeks to cut layers and simplify teams

Only around 1% of staff to remain remote

Focus shifts towards robotaxis and AI

Uber Technologies will cut about 3,300 jobs, representing roughly 10% of its global workforce, as part of a major restructuring aimed at reducing management layers and reallocating resources towards its core ride-hailing, delivery and robotaxi businesses.The job cuts will reduce the number of managers at the company by 20%, chief executive officer Dara Khosrowshahi said in an email to employees.An Uber spokesperson said some managers would be moved into individual contributor roles, while the layoffs would also affect employees who are not managers.Uber had about 34,000 employees globally at the end of last year, according to its annual report cited by Reuters.Khosrowshahi said Uber's rapid growth over the past five years had created greater complexity within the company.“Over the last 5+ years, Uber has grown by orders of magnitude, with our top line nearly tripling,” he wrote in the email, which was obtained by Bloomberg News.“But that growth has also brought complexity: more layers, more coordination, more fragmented ownership, and in some cases structures that made sense when businesses were smaller but no longer serve us well at our current scale.”The restructuring is aimed at making the company “simpler and faster”, Khosrowshahi said.Uber has reduced roles primarily focused on coordination and broadened managers' responsibilities, particularly in teams with only one or two direct reports.According to Khosrowshahi's email, the number of employees sitting seven or more layers below the CEO has been reduced by 20%, while the number of such small teams, or “micro-teams”, has been cut by nearly 50%.The company is also combining teams where it believes fragmentation has created duplication and slowed decision-making. Uber will merge its three Delivery Operations teams covering restaurants, retail and Direct into single teams at the global, regional and country levels.Its Core Services Engineering and Science teams are also being combined, Bloomberg reported.Uber is also tightening its location and remote-work policies as part of the overhaul.The company will concentrate global teams in its largest global hubs in New York and San Francisco, while regional, local and technology teams will be based in designated hubs.The company is asking the vast majority of remote employees to move to an office. Going forward, only around 1% of Uber's employees will be allowed to work remotely, while the company will continue to enforce its hybrid policy requiring staff to work from the office three days a week.Khosrowshahi said the savings from the restructuring would be reinvested in growth, innovation and other capabilities.“Our opportunity from here is enormous: we have the chance to bring Uber to hundreds of millions more people; to invest even more in drivers, couriers and merchants; and to innovate across our core businesses and build the autonomous future,” he said.The restructuring comes as Uber has pledged to commit more than $10 billion to robotaxi partnerships in the coming years.The company has also invested in Avride Inc., Lucid Group Inc., Nuro Inc. and Rivian Automotive Inc., while reallocating capital by reducing stakes in some other companies.The latest layoffs follow more targeted job cuts Uber made this year in its customer service and human resources departments. Unlike several major technology companies, Uber had avoided large-scale workforce reductions since the Covid-19 pandemic.Uber said in May that it would moderate the pace of hiring. Wednesday's cuts will bring the company's total employee count to just under 30,000.Khosrowshahi did not mention artificial intelligence as a reason for the restructuring in his announcement, though Bloomberg reported that the changes were also being driven by Uber's efforts to use more AI technology in its daily operations.Uber's shares rose 2% following the announcement.
Article Summary: Uber will cut about 3,300 jobs, representing roughly 10% of its global workforce. The job cuts will reduce the number of managers at the company by 20%, chief executive officer Dara Khosrowshahi said in an email to employees. Only around 1% of staff will be allowed to work remotely, while the company will continue to enforce its hybrid policy.

Article Title: Oil climbs past $90 as Middle East conflict keeps Strait of Hormuz shut
Article Text:
Crude prices continue to jump as Middle East tensions intensify

Oil prices inched higher on Tuesday after renewed tensions between the US and Iran brought the risk of supply disruptions in the Middle East back to the forefront.Brent crude rose 55 cents, or 0.61%, to $91.04 while WTI crude was up 79 cents, or 0.92%, at $86.55 a barrel, around 7:30 am IST.The latest rise came after a sharp jump in the previous session. Brent ended Monday 2.7% higher, having earlier touched its strongest level since August 25. WTI settled 2.8% higher after reaching its highest since August 21.The renewed concerns followed the first direct exchange of attacks between the US and Iran in a month on Sunday. US President Donald Trump on Monday threatened further strikes against Iran, escalating tensions after the conflict had recently shifted towards an economic standoff.For oil markets, the situation around the Strait of Hormuz remains a key concern. Only five visible commodity vessels a day were seen transiting the waterway over the weekend, according to shipping data from Kpler.The strait carried about a fifth of global oil supplies before the war began in late February. Iran closed the waterway after the US and Israel attacked the country on February 28.Mediation efforts by Qatar and Oman to secure a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz have so far failed to gain traction.The continuing uncertainty around shipping was underscored on Tuesday when the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations agency (UKMTO) said a tanker had reported being struck by three projectiles while sailing out of the strait. There were no casualties or environmental impact reported.Alongside the disruption risks in the Middle East, developments in Venezuela are also in focus as the US looks to replenish its oil reserves. Trump announced a deal with Venezuela on Friday to control oil reserves in the country and later said it would help replenish the US Strategic Petroleum Reserve, which is near a 44-year low.Energy companies are also moving towards agreements on projects in Venezuela. Indian oil giant ONGC, Chevron and GE Vernova of the US, Italy's Eni and Colombia's GeoPark are on track to sign final agreements after months of negotiations to firm up energy projects in the OPEC country, five sources close to the preparations said on Monday.The Strategic Petroleum Reserve itself fell further last week, with crude inventories declining by about 3.1 million barrels to 286.6 million barrels.With shipping disruptions continuing, analysts polled by Reuters in August expect oil prices to stay above $80 a barrel in 2026.
Article Summary: Brent crude rose 55 cents, or 0.61%, to $91.04 while WTI crude was up 79 cents, at $86.55 a barrel. The latest rise came after a sharp jump in the previous session. Brent ended Monday 2.7% higher, having earlier touched its strongest level since August 25.

Article Title: UAE, Egypt coordinate over Banque Misr bank after US Treasury notice on Iran links, dollar curbs
Article Text:
Egypt's Banque Misr is reviewing US sanctions targeting its UAE branches for alleged Iran dealings

The United Arab Emirates and Egyptian central banks are coordinating over Banque Misr after the US Treasury proposed cutting off the Egyptian bank’s UAE branches from dollar transactions over alleged financial links to Iran.In a joint statement on Sunday, the two central banks said Banque Misr would take “all necessary measures” to continue its business as usual, reported Reuters.The proposed US measure is expected to take effect less than 30 days after a public comment period. It applies only to Banque Misr’s UAE branches and would prevent them from carrying out transactions in US dollars through the US financial system.Banque Misr said on Saturday that it was reviewing the US Treasury notice.The move comes as Washington steps up pressure on banks and financial institutions seen as facilitating Iran’s access to the global financial system.Meanwhile, US treasury secretary Scott Bessent told Reuters on Sunday that the department was likely to announce new secondary sanctions against Iran-linked entities every week, with banks an initial focus.“You're going to see a lot more of these every week,” Bessent said, warning banks that “it’s not okay to have Iranian money and to aid the regime.”“There can be no leakage,” Bessent added, “You're either with us or you're with the Iranians.”The Treasury launched the campaign, dubbed “Operation Economic Outcast”, last week, saying it aims to cut off the financial networks that help Iran generate revenue, evade sanctions and fund its activities.This came as the US treasury alleged on Friday that Banque Misr UAE had processed about $1.8 billion for 103 companies potentially linked to Iranian shadow-banking networks between January 2024 and June 2026.The Treasury described the UAE operation as a “critical node” in Iran’s access to US dollars and said some of the bank’s customers included apparent front companies used by Iran’s Ministry of Defence and Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps to evade sanctions.The proposed rule would prohibit US financial institutions from maintaining correspondent accounts for Banque Misr UAE and require them to take steps to prevent transactions involving the UAE bank from being processed through the US financial system.The Treasury stressed that the proposed measure applies only to Banque Misr UAE and not to the bank’s operations in other countries.Bessent said the next stage of the campaign could involve cutting institutions off entirely from the dollar-based financial system, while urging G20 finance ministers and central bank governors to sever economic ties with Iran or risk secondary sanctions.The US has also imposed sanctions on Reza Mohammad Taeedi, manager of Bank Melli’s Dubai branch, and a Hong Kong-based company accused of helping sanctioned Iranian entities access the international financial system.
Article Summary: Egypt's Banque Misr is reviewing US sanctions targeting its UAE branches for alleged Iran dealings. The US Treasury proposed cutting off the Egyptian bank’s UAE branches from dollar transactions over alleged financial links to Iran. The proposed US measure is expected to take effect less than 30 days after a public comment period.

Article Title: China trade portfolio: Factory activity contracts in August despite stronger export demand
Article Text:
China's factory activity contracts in August despite stronger export demand

Domestic economy remains under pressure

Exports remain a key support

China’s factory activity showed signs of stabilisation in August as stronger overseas demand helped lift new orders and production, although manufacturing remained below the level that signals growth. The official manufacturing purchasing managers’ index (PMI) rose to 49.8 in August from 49.2 in July, the National Bureau of Statistics said on Monday. The reading was better than economists had forecast, but remained below the 50-mark that separates expansion from contraction.PMI readings are based on monthly surveys of companies and range from 0 to 100. A reading above 50 indicates an expansion in activity, while a reading below 50 points to a contraction.The improvement was driven in part by a recovery in demand from overseas markets.“Manufacturing activity rebounded thanks to strong export demand,” Nguyen Hoang Nam, a China economist at Capital Economics, wrote in a research note Monday.The underlying factory data also showed a broader improvement. The production sub-index moved above the 50-mark, rising to 50.4 in August from 49.9 in July. New orders climbed to 50.6 from 48.5, while new export orders edged up to 50.1 from 49.6.Huo Lihui, a chief statistician with the national bureau of statistics, said in a statement that the August PMI data reflected an improvement in China's overall economy.The improvement in factory activity has come against a backdrop of weaker domestic demand. China’s prolonged property-sector slump has partly contributed to sluggish demand at home, weighing on the broader economy despite the strength of exports.China’s economy grew at an annual pace of 4.3% in the April-June quarter. That was the slowest growth rate recorded in more than three years.China’s export performance has remained strong despite pressure on trade with the US. Exports rose almost 24% in July from a year earlier and increased more than 18% in the first seven months of the year.High-tech goods, including semiconductors, have benefited from strong demand linked to the boom in artificial intelligence. Electric vehicles have also been an important source of export growth, with demand partly supported by higher energy costs due to the Iran war.At the same time, Chinese exporters have been selling more to markets such as Europe and Southeast Asia as US tariffs have dented China-US trade following Donald Trump’s return to the White House last year.“ Demand for green technologies was already accelerating last year and has continued to strengthen, providing an important additional boost to Chinese exports so far this year,” said Max Zenglein, a senior economist for the Asia Pacific at The Conference Board.Trade is also expected to remain a key issue in discussions between Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping, who are expected to meet in late September.
Article Summary: Official manufacturing purchasing managers’ index (PMI) rose to 49.8 in August from 49.2 in July. The reading was better than economists had forecast, but remained below the 50-mark that separates expansion from contraction. The improvement was driven in part by a recovery in demand from overseas markets. China’s prolonged property-sector slump has partly contributed to sluggish demand at home.

Article Title: Iran war at 6 months: Who gained, who lost the most economically
Article Text:
Motorcyclists ride past a billboard depicting US President Donald Trump inside a catering container in downtown Tehran, Iran

Winners

1. Investors who stayed calm

2. Clean energy and electric vehicles

3. US defence contractors

Losers

1. Airlines and travellers

2. Farmers and the fight against hunger

3. Consumers and import-dependent economies

Six months into the war between the US, Israel and Iran, some of the worst fears for the global economy have failed to materialise, despite the conflict driving up energy and food costs, disrupting travel and trade, and adding to pressure on already fragile supply chains.Oil prices surged after the US and Israel began military action against Iran on February 28, with Brent crude rising from around $72 a barrel before the war to nearly $120 at its peak as shipping through the Strait of Hormuz was disrupted. Prices have since eased, although they remain above pre-war levels.Financial markets, meanwhile, have recovered sharply from the initial shock.
